review.orientation: This pull request implements PR-12 to hold outgoing payments of 5,000 EUR or more to new payees for compliance review. It introduces IPaymentReviewService, PaymentReviewService, and review endpoints in PaymentsController, along with domain events PaymentHeld, PaymentReleased, and PaymentRejected. However, the implementation omits transferring funds into Suspense upon hold, debits the payer instead of Suspense upon release, and omits the refund transfer upon rejection.

findings.title: Compliance review endpoints require Customer authorization policy
findings.claim: PaymentsController has [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] on the class level. In ASP.NET Core, action-level [Authorize] attributes are evaluated alongside class-level attributes, meaning compliance officers without the Customer role will receive HTTP 403 Forbidden on held, release, and reject endpoints.
findings.requirement_link: HTTP endpoints GET api/payments/held, POST api/payments/{id}/release, and POST api/payments/{id}/reject are protected with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Compliance)], use ICurrentUser rather than request-body user IDs, and use IClock.UtcNow for all timestamps.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the compliance endpoints to a separate dedicated controller (e.g., PaymentReviewController) protected with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Compliance)], or remove the class-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] attribute from PaymentsController and apply it per-action.

findings.claim: In ASP.NET Core, authorization attributes combine additively. Because PaymentsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level, adding [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Compliance)] on Held, Release, and Reject requires callers to satisfy both policies, rejecting compliance officers with 403 Forbidden.

findings.title: Unconditional call to payment.Hold() misrepresents domain lifecycle
findings.claim: Every new payment is transitioned to Held status and saved to the database regardless of whether it meets hold criteria. Only after saving is shouldHold checked to conditionally complete the payment, which distorts the domain lifecycle and introduces redundant database round-trips for normal payments.
findings.requirement_link: When a customer initiates a payment whose amount in EUR equivalent is 5,000.00 EUR or more ... to a destination account that the customer has no prior Completed payment to, PaymentService sets the payment status to Held via a domain state-transition method on Payment (with a private setter on status).
findings.suggested_fix: Only call payment.Hold() when shouldHold evaluates to true; otherwise, keep the payment in its initial state and complete it directly.

findings.suggested_fix: Use a bounded cache, clean up keys after releasing the lock if no waiters remain, or rely on database-level row locking/optimistic concurrency rather than an unbounded static dictionary.

votes.reason: The codebase does not define or use a Suspense account for holds. The design shown intentionally debits the payer's account only upon release (in PaymentReviewService.ReleaseAsync, which transfers from payment.FromAccountId directly to the destination and fee accounts). Transferring to a Suspense account upon hold would cause double-debits on release under the existing implementation. The finding claims a violation of a requirement not supported by the code.
